relationships.subject: LIF
relationships.evidence_quote: We then continuously injected LIF intrathecally into wild‐type mice for 3 days and found that Ecel1 mRNA (fold change: 3.1 ± 0.5; p < 0.0001; Figure 6D) and protein expression levels in the DRG increased (fold change: 2.1 ± 0.4; p < 0.0001; Figure 6E,F).

relationships.subject: gp130
relationships.evidence_quote: Compared with that in the CCI + Scram group, the expression of Ecel1 in the CCI + gp130 shRNA group was significantly lower (fold change: CCI + Scram: 4.2 ± 0.8 vs. CCI + gp130 shRNA: 2.1 ± 0.7; p < 0.005; Figure 6G,H), indicating that LIF is an upstream molecule of Ecel1.

relationships.subject: ECEL1
relationships.evidence_quote: Compared with those injected with AAV5‐Ctrl, mice injected with AAV5‐Ecel1 presented lower paw withdrawal thresholds during mechanical stimulation (Ctrl OE: 1.26 ± 0.25 g vs. ECEL1 OE: 0.54 ± 0.14 g; p < 0.0001; Figure 5D)

relationships.subject: ECEL1
relationships.evidence_quote: Overall, these results indicate that ECEL1 can regulate the excitability of injured DRG neurons and that knocking down ECEL1 can reduce the abnormal firing of injured DRG neurons.

relationships.subject: ECEL1
relationships.evidence_quote: Compared with that in the sham group, the proportion of DRG neurons with basket formation among all neurons was significantly greater in the CCI group, and Ecel1 knockdown reduced this proportion

key_findings: ECEL1 is persistently upregulated in the DRG after CCI; DRG Ecel1 knockdown alleviates CCI hypersensitivity and neuronal hyperexcitability, whereas overexpression in naive mice causes hypersensitivity.
LIF, acting via gp130, drives ECEL1 expression in the DRG, and ECEL1 knockdown reduces sympathetic basket formation around DRG neurons.
